explanation: An important Jewish festival celebrating the liberation of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt.
Bread made without yeast, eaten during Passover to remember the haste with which the Israelites left Egypt.
The first and best harvests offered to God as a sign of gratitude and honor.
Every seventh year when the land was to rest and not be cultivated, so that the poor and animals could eat what grew naturally.
A seven-day harvest festival during which the Israelites lived in shelters to remember their journey through the wilderness after being freed from Egypt.
A person chosen by God to lead and judge the Israelites with justice.
A gift or act given to God to express gratitude, reverence, or to seek atonement for sins.
